A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FlowTok research, and their text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison. v1 includes Appendices A–C; these are absent from the complete supplied v3 PDF, rather than relocated or unreadable.

before.justification: v1 reports original text-to-image and image-captioning results, tokenizer evaluation and alignment-loss ablations in Sections 5.1–5.3. Appendix B supplies additional generated images and captions.

after.justification: v3 retains the original tokenizer, generation, captioning and ablation results in Sections 5.1–5.3 and Tables 2–4.

M1.justification: Both versions retain the same 77×16 latent representation, RoPE/SwiGLU-enhanced image tokenizer, text projector and decoder, DiT flow-matching architecture, and training losses. Removing implementation documentation does not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: The training datasets and evaluated tasks remain unchanged: both use the same DataComp, CC12M, LAION, JourneyDB and DALLE3-1M sources, with COCO, MJHQ-30K and ImageNet evaluations. Removed qualitative examples illustrate existing tasks without establishing distinct test scenarios.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 retain the same comparator sets, including CrossFlow, PixArt-α and Show-o for image generation, and CrossFlow, MNIC, MIR, NAIC-CMAL, SATIC and SCD-Net for captioning. Newly cited works are not added to these comparisons.

E3.justification: The stated COCO split, evaluation metrics, default 20 sampling steps, model configurations, 256px throughput protocol and ablations without CFG remain unchanged. Omission of Appendix A removes setting documentation but does not report a revised experimental procedure.

E4.justification: Appendix B's qualitative evidence concerning image diversity/fidelity and correspondence between images and generated captions disappears with Figures 5–8. The controlled alignment-target, loss-function and loss-weight ablations in Section 5.3 and Table 4 remain identical.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for the experiments. The reporting practice remains single-valued results.

E6.justification: v3 removes the additional generated-image galleries and eight captioning examples in Figures 5–8. Quantitative outcomes remain unchanged, including FlowTok-H's COCO/MJHQ-30K FIDs of 9.67/7.15, FlowTok-XL's captioning CIDEr of 117.0, and every Table 4 ablation value.

T1.justification: The latent-space definitions, interpolation and velocity equations, contrastive alignment loss and combined training objective are mathematically unchanged. Neither version adds or removes a theorem, proof or substantive derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: direct bidirectional flow between compact text/image tokens, reduced resource requirements, faster sampling and competitive generation quality. The code-release update changes access information rather than the scientific claims.

C2.justification: v3 removes Appendix C's substantive limitations discussion: unavoidable semantic loss from text compression, potentially weaker text–image alignment than cross-attention models, and proposed remedies involving stronger alignment or larger latent channels. Discussion of unexplored flow-matching refinements also disappears; main-text result interpretations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Removing Appendix A and Tables 5–6 eliminates dataset-specific filtering and recaptioning instructions, optimizer settings, learning rates, warmup, batch sizes and training-step counts. Conversely, the abstract changes code from promised at bytedance/1d-tokenizer to reported available at TACJu/FlowTok; repository contents cannot be assessed from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v3 adds four background works, including ReVision and Deeply Supervised Flow-Based Generative Models, replaces the self-supervised SiT reference with the generative SiT paper, and removes two appendix-only LAION tool references. Duplicate references are consolidated. The central positioning relative to CrossFlow and 1D tokenizers remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Sections 1–6 retain their sequence and nearly all wording. v3 removes the appendix structure, updates code-release wording and makes small citation edits. Section 5.1 still directs readers to an appendix that is no longer included.

P2.justification: v3 removes both detailed training tables, Tables 5–6, and all four supplementary visual displays, Figures 5–8. This substantially reduces the technical and qualitative presentation. Main-text Figures 1–4 and Tables 1–4 remain essentially unchanged.

improvement.justification: The quantitative evidence and scientific core remain intact, and the reported code release and citation corrections are useful improvements. However, v3 removes the explicit data-curation and training recipe in Appendix A and the central semantic-compression limitation in Appendix C, without replacements in the supplied PDF. These losses substantially weaken reproducibility and qualification of the unchanged claims; the removed qualitative examples further reduce supporting evidence.
